Judgment :

1. By invoking Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India, petitioners, who are original respondents in L.A.R. No.04 of 2010 (old L.A.R. No.458 of 2010), are hereby taking exception to the judgment and order passed by learned Civil Judge, Senior Division, Kandhar, Dist. Nanded.
Learned counsel Shri Anerao points out that, petitioners are original claimants in L.A.R. No.04 of 2010 before the Civil Judge, Senior Division, Kandhar.

That, respondent - Special Land Acquisition Officer, PT & MIW No.2, Nanded (acquiring body) was pleased to acquire their land admeasuring 2H 82R out of Gut No. 122 for storage back water at village Nandanshivani, Tq. Kandhar, Dist.

sentences.text: Nanded.

3. It is further pointed out that, after due measurement, respondent - acquiring body passed final award to the tune of Rs.1,18,000/- per Hector i.e. on account of acquisition of petitioner's land admeasuring 2H 81R out of Gut No.122 and even compensation amount to the tune of Rs.5,05,795/-
was awarded.

However, reference was made under section 30 of Land Acquisition Act, to decide,
who is the actual claimant and beneficiary, as there was a dispute regarding ownership, possession and entitlement of compensation, the respondent acquiring body instituted proceedings under section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act to decide the apportionment of compensation asserted by various parties.
4. It is further pointed out that, before the said Court, the Special Land Acquisition Officer has placed on record a copy of E-statement and Award.
Present petitioners had obtained photocopies of the same and they had placed it on record.
However, learned trial Court held that, said documents are xerox copies and not certified copies.
That, on such count WP-2713-2015 itself, reference has been dismissed.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, they are ready to procure a certificated copy of E-Statement and to approach the learned trial Court for fresh determination of the issue of apportionment and accordingly he prays to remand the matter back.
6.
Learned APP also pointed out that, only because of xerox copies of E-statement were placed on record, the learned trial Court refused to rely on the same and dismissed the matter.

He has no objection, if petitioners undertake to obtain certified copies of E-statement, 7/12 extract and other relevant documents and approach the Civil Court afresh for a decision of the entitlement of apportionment on merits.

7. Therefore, in view of the above limited prayers and in the interest of justice, as admittedly there is no dispute that the land of the petitioners is already acquired and the compensation determined by the authorities has already been deposited before the learned trial Court for decision on apportionment, the petitioners are permitted to approach the learned trial Court afresh with certified copies of E-statement, 7/12 extracts and other relevant documents for a decision under section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Hence, the following order is passed :
WP-2713-2015 ORDER
(i) The impugned judgment and order dated 01.04.2014 passed by learned Civil Judge, Senior Division, Kandhar in L.A.R. NO.04 of 2010 (Old L.A.R. No.458 fo 2010) is hereby set aside.

(ii) Matter is remanded back to the file of learned Civil Judge, Senior Division,
Kandhar.

Learned Civil Judge Senior Division, Kandhar to permit petitioners to place on record certified copies of E-statement, 7/12 extract, and other relevant documents for substantiating their claim over the apportionment of compensation deposited in Madhukar Govindrao Deokate And Others vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer, ... on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108704317/
